Hi, Autocar India, Currently, I have the 2020 Venue diesel. Now I, want an electric SUV. Also, I like XEV 9S but I am skeptical about waiting for BE7 but idk if i should wait or not also its easy for me to buy XEV9S with BAAS. Please suggest, should I wait for BE7 or buy XEV9S?
The XEV 9S is already on sale, offers strong performance and plenty of space, and BaaS reduces the upfront cost by separating the battery financing from the vehicle. Just remember that the battery cost is still payable through a separate finance arrangement, so compare the total outgo over your intended ownership period.The BE 07 is expected to launch in 2027 and will be a five seater, positioned above the BE 6. It is likely to share the existing INGLO platform and battery options, but its final price, range and specifications are not confirmed. Since you are coming from a Venue diesel, the XEV 9S will be a substantial upgrade in space and performance.
Currently, I own a Kia Sonet Diesel Manual and Scorpio N diesel manual. I want to replace Scorpio N diesel manual with a mid-size SUV EV. So, I’m waiting for the Mahindra BE 07 since the XEV 9e is too big for my daily commute and the Mahindra BE 6 isn’t suitable for a family. I am replacing my Scorpio N because there’s too much traffic in the city, parking constraints, and that car is huge, and I want to drive something smaller for daily commute. My usage is 70% within city and 30% within highway.
You are making the right call moving away from the Scorpio N. It is ok as a highway SUV, but in dense city traffic and tight parking, its size becomes a daily headache. The XEV 9e would put you in exactly the same situation, so it is not the right replacement. The BE 6 is a good EV, but it is more of a coupe-style SUV with a sloping roofline, which compromises rear headroom and practicality for family use.The BE 07 is the right car to wait for. It is Mahindra’s upcoming flagship EV and is expected to be a proper midsize SUV with a more practical, family-friendly cabin. It should offer the right balance of size, space and EV performance for your 70:30 city-highway usage. The only caveat is timing - if you need a car soon, the BE 07 may not arrive quickly enough.If you want an alternative that is available now, the Hyundai Creta EV is a very good option. It is spacious and practical EV with a comfortable ride and a family-friendly cabin. It is not as rugged as the Scorpio N, but for city commuting and occasional highway runs, it is a very well-rounded package, moreover the electronics and powertrain are very well calibrated making for a fuss free and easy drive experience and with very good reliability. Not something todays current EVs can boast off. Overall, your thinking is correct: the BE 7 is the right size and type of EV to replace a Scorpio N for city-focused family use. If you can wait, it is worth holding out for to see if it shapes up well. If not, electric Hyundai Creta is the best available alternative at the moment.
